newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas rises on storage refills.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas rises on storage refills.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices moved higher Thursday as storage injections escalated in western Canada, industry sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, swing prices rose by two to four cents to about C$1.50-1.51 per gigajoule (GJ) despite continued mild weather in Alberta.
"NOVA is in good shape, and storage injections are starting to go in at a steady pace," one Calgary-based source said, noting injections into the hub on Wednesday totalled 369 million cubic feet.
Canadian Gas Association said Thursday stocks in the West as of March 21 were at 43.52 bcf, 16.8 percent full, compared with a year ago when storage was at 27.1 percent of capacity.
April AECO prices were also higher at C$1.52-1.55 per GJ.
At Sumas, Wash., next-day prices climbed into the low-to-mid $1.20s per million British thermal units (mmBtu), up about six cents from Wednesday's levels.
Meanwhile, April prices converged closer to the daily market at $1.20.
At Niagara, swing prices were unchanged at $2.15 per mmBtu, while April prices climbed two cents to meet March at $2.15.

Overall, gas stocks in Canada as of March 21 were at 57.36 bcf, or 11.67 percent full. Year-ago levels were at 17.3 percent of capacity. In the East, stocks dipped below year-ago levels to 13.84 bcf, or 5.95 percent full.
